title: N-S-A
hook: nasa: to lift, to carry, as in Naso

segments.voice: Yesterday, A-R-V: erev, evening, and arev, the one who stands surety. Your line was we stand surety. Whose side did you stand on? Today's root is the lifting itself. Day one thousand four hundred twenty-one.

When the Torah counts people, it doesn't always use a word for counting. In the portion called Naso, God tells Moses: "Take also the sum of the sons of Gershon." The Hebrew is naso et rosh: lift up the head. To count someone, in that phrasing, is to raise their head, to see each face, one at a time. Later in the same portion comes a blessing that lifts something else: "The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace." Today's root does the lifting in both.
screen: `NASO: LIFT UP THE HEAD.` → `EACH FACE, ONE AT A TIME.` → `LIFT UP HIS COUNTENANCE.`

segments.voice: N-S-A. Nun, sin, alef. Nasa: to lift, to carry, to bear. Turn it a few ways. First, the eyes. "I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help." I will lift is essa, from this root. Lifting begins with where you look. Second, the shoulders. In the same portion, Naso, the Levites of Kohath carry the holy things of the sanctuary, and the text says they bore them upon their shoulders: the same verb. The leaders of the tribes in that portion are called nesi'im, from these letters too. Third, forgiveness. When God's attributes are proclaimed to Moses, one of them is "forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin." The Hebrew for forgiving there is nosei: carrying. To forgive, in this root, is to lift a wrong off someone and bear it. Cain uses the same verb from the other side, in despair: "My punishment is greater than I can bear." Too heavy to lift. Fourth, the hands. When the priests bless the people with the words from Naso, the practice is called nesiat kapayim, the lifting of the hands. So one root raises heads to be counted, eyes to the hills, holy things onto shoulders, wrongs off backs, and hands in blessing. In this root, lifting and carrying and forgiving are one motion.
screen: `I WILL LIFT UP MINE EYES.` · `HOLY THINGS ON THEIR SHOULDERS.` · `FORGIVING IS CARRYING.` · `THE LIFTING OF THE HANDS.` · then, large: `ONE MOTION: LIFT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: lift one burden. Settle, and breathe. Let your shoulders rise on an in-breath and drop on the out-breath. Do that a few times, slowly. Then ask: what is someone near me carrying that I could lift, even a little? A chore, an errand, a worry, a grudge you could set down. Or a weight of your own you could put down for the length of the bell. Choose one. Notice your shoulders as you choose. If you pray, you can say the psalm's line: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills. The bell holds the time.
screen: `SHOULDERS UP, SHOULDERS DOWN.` · `WHAT COULD I LIFT?` · `CHOOSE ONE.`

segments.voice: N-S-A. Nun, sin, alef: nasa, to lift, to carry, to forgive. And this week's lines, in order: the world hides, exile reveals, sit and learn, friendship joins, dawn, we stand surety, lift. Today's word.
Your line: lift. Today, pick up one thing someone else was carrying, a bag, a task, a mistake, and carry it a little way for them. Day one thousand four hundred twenty-one.

howItsDone: The Torah portion Naso (Numbers 4:21–7:89) takes its name from 'naso et rosh', lift up the head; it includes the priestly blessing, which the priests give with raised hands, nesiat kapayim. Exodus 34:7 uses the same verb for forgiving.

fork.setup: you're Cain, sentenced to wander the earth. what do you say to God?
options: my punishment is greater than I can bear.
fork.reveal: "My punishment is greater than I can bear": too heavy to lift, with today's verb. and God sets a mark on him, so that no one would kill him.

original.note: Hebrew: to lift, carry, bear, from nun, sin, alef; Naso, 'lift up', names a Torah portion.

trapdoor: what you thought: nasa just means to pick something up.
what it means: N-S-A lifts heads to be counted, eyes to the hills, holy things onto shoulders, and hands in blessing.
what a scholar hears: nosei in Exodus 34:7, forgiveness as carrying; and nesiat kapayim, the priests' lifted hands.
